title: Scheduler scorecards and lightweight in-line probes for per-kernel latency attribution
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem / Context: Current runtime telemetry provides detailed kernel-level metrics via sampled spans and NVTX ranges, but attribution between scheduler decisions (prefill vs decode handoffs, microbatch assignment) and observed per-kernel latencies is noisy. Root-cause work is slow because engineers must stitch traces and manually recompute per-request scoring.

Goal: Add a lightweight in-line probing layer ("mini-probes") and a scheduler scorecard emit path to produce deterministic, low-overhead per-request and per-kernel attribution. The output should enable: (1) accurate attribution of latency to scheduler actions (batch selection, kernel variant choice), (2) high-cardinality rollups for cost vs latency dashboards, and (3) fast local debugging without heavy trace lookups.

Scope & approach:
- Mini-probes: micro-timers (wall-clock) inserted at scheduler handoff points and kernel dispatch boundaries. Probes emit: probe_id, event_type (SCHED_HANOFF, KERNEL_DISPATCH, KERNEL_COMPLETE), kernel_variant, queue_depth, microbatch_id, and latency_ms. Probes will be implemented as optional fast-path code guarded by a runtime-config flag.
- NVTX complement: Each mini-probe will also optionally push an NVTX range for compatibility with existing trace correlation. NVTX range names will follow the pattern: "rs:score:<probe_id>:<event_type>" to avoid collisions with existing naming.
- Scorecards: The scheduler will assemble per-request scorecards (small arrays of probe summaries) and emit a concise protobuf-ish flattened line to our metrics collector (via the existing sidecar batching channel). Scorecards are bounded to N entries (default 6) to cap overhead.
- Sampling & rollout: Default sampling rate 5% per request; full sampling enabled for debug toggles. Progressive rollout via runtime flag (10% -> 50% -> 100%) to monitor overhead.
- Aggregation & dashboards: New Datadog metrics: runtime.scheduler.score.latency_p50/p95, runtime.kernel.variant.latency_p50/p95, runtime.scheduler.queue_depth.avg. Scorecards additionally emit labeled logs to S3 for offline cohorting and per-model analysis.

Trade-offs considered:
- Wall-clock timers are easier to interpret for scheduling latency than GPU kernel timestamps but are susceptible to host scheduling noise. To mitigate, we record CPU affinity and, when available, GPU exec-id to correlate.
- NVTX push/pop per small probe increases NVTX churn; we keep NVTX on only for full sampling or when NVTX-compatible tracing is explicitly required.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Instrument scheduler code paths with mini-probes and internal in-memory scorecard assembly (feature-flagged).
2) Add an efficient emission path to the sidecar collector (protobuf flattened line) with bounded batching.
3) Implement Datadog metric mapping and a lightweight Kinesis/S3 log sink for scorecard lines.
4) Add NVTX range name mapping and opt-in behavior.
5) End-to-end test: run perf bench suite (prefill/decode mix) at 0/5/50/100% sampling, measure CPU overhead, NVTX throughput, and correlation quality.
6) Dashboard and alerting: create default dashboards and a 'scorecard-regression' alert (10% increase in p95 attributed to scheduler).

Acceptance criteria:
- Instrumentation adds <=2% median p99 increase in end-to-end latency at 5% sampling on our standard perf cluster.
- Scorecard lines are emitted and ingested to the collector within 30s of request completion for 95% of samples.
- New Datadog metrics show stable baselines and correlate with trace-derived attribution in at least 90% of sampled traces.
- NVTX ranges use the new naming schema and can be filtered by the trace viewer without colliding with pre-existing ranges.

Rollout & monitoring:
- Start 10% sampling in canary region (us-west-2) for 48h. Monitor cpu_utilization, sidecar queue length, NVTX range rate, and disk/bandwidth for S3 sink.
- If overhead <1.5% increase across medians and errors <0.1%, increase to 50% then 100% following successful validation windows.

comments: 2026-02-22: Spike completed. Micro-timer insertion proof-of-concept shows low overhead on single-threaded decode; details in spike notes.

2026-02-27: Design sync with infra and telemetry teams. Decided to reuse sidecar batching channel and to keep scorecard lines compact (ASCII flattened). Action: Marco to draft emission protobuf schema.
2026-03-03: Implemented FFI for mini-probe record type and added runtime flag. Local perf run (5% sampling) shows ~0.7% p50 latency increase, ~1.1% p95. NVTX optionality implemented.

2026-03-08: Integration tests failing on high-concurrency path: sidecar batches occasionally exceed 512KB. Mitigation: introduce per-request size limit and batch flush on size threshold. Patch in PR #1428.

2026-03-12: Canaries deployed to us-west-2 at 10% sampling. Observed 1.3% median latency increase and scorecard ingestion latency median 12s. Next: monitor for 48h and validate correlation against existing traces.
